territorial_scope.description: Applies to institutions authorised by the Central Bank of Brazil and, through contracting conditions, reaches cloud services provided abroad.

evidence.quote: prestados no exterior

summary.short: Requires Central Bank-authorised payment institutions (and, as amended, certain brokers and virtual asset providers) to adopt a cybersecurity policy and incident plan and follow rules for contracting cloud and data-processing services, including notification and conditions for services abroad. Applies from 1 August 2021.
summary.long: Sets cybersecurity policy and cloud-contracting rules for payment institutions and, under later amendments, certain securities brokers and distributors, foreign-exchange brokers and virtual asset service providers authorised by the Central Bank of Brazil. Each institution must adopt a cybersecurity policy with minimum contents, approved by its board and reviewed annually, plus an incident response plan; it must publish a policy summary, designate a responsible director and report annually on the plan. Before contracting relevant cloud or data-processing services, it must follow verification procedures, include specified contract clauses, and notify the Central Bank within ten days. Services provided abroad require a Central Bank information-sharing agreement with the foreign supervisor or prior Central Bank authorisation requested sixty days in advance. The Central Bank may veto or restrict contracting for non-compliance. Records must be kept for five years. The Resolution took effect on 1 August 2021; the text reflects amendments by Resolutions 368/2024, 538/2025 and 552/2026.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff changing legal treatment found. Time periods (ten days for communications in Art. 15 §§ 2-3; thirty days for interruption notice in Art. 17 parágrafo único II; sixty days for prior authorisation in Art. 16 § 1) are procedural deadlines coded as events. The five-year retention period (Art. 23) is an obligation. The 1 September 2019 cohort date in Art. 24 is revoked and is not a numeric threshold. Art. 25 and the relevance criteria in Art. 12 § 1 contain no numeric value.
